source_title: Govt tables Rs 7,844 cr supplementary budget, provisions for Kumbh, Gairsain - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Gairsain: Uttarakhand govt has tabled a Rs 7,884 crore supplementary budget in the state assembly on Tuesday; out of which, provision of Rs 3,679 crore has been kept under the revenue head and Rs 4,164 crore under capital head. Earlier, during the budget session in March, the state assembly had passed a Rs 1.11 lakh crore budget.Besides, there were nine other Bills, including the Uttarakhand Irrigation Bill 2026, which will replace the 153-year old Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873. The assembly also paid tributes to ex-CM Major Gen BC Khanduri and ex-Cabinet minister Hira Singh Bisht.A key provision in the supplementary budget was a Rs 290 crore provision for Kumbh, which is scheduled to commence from Jan 2027. In view of upcoming Kumbh, the govt has allocated Rs 30 crore for Haridwar-Ganga corridor project.For the Gairsain water supply dam project, a provision of Rs 122 crore has been kept. For the payment of contractors under Jal Jeevan Mission, Rs 300 crore has been earmarked. For procurement of paddy and wheat, the govt has kept Rs 1,100 crore. Rs 160 crore has been kept for the medical and nursing college in Pithoragarh.As prize money for international medal winners, a provision of Rs 15 crore has been kept. For sports university, govt has kept a budget of Rs 35 crore.The supplementary budget has several provisions for women as well including Rs 20 crore for honorarium to Bhojan Mata, Rs 20 crore for anganwadi and nutrition and Rs 27 crore under destitute widow pension.CM Pushkar Singh Dhami said that several important provisions have been included in the supplementary budget. âWeâve made allocation for Kumbh-related works and projects for Gairsain,â Dhami added.Paying tributes to late Khanduri, who died on May 19 this year, Dhami in the House said, âHe was not only the hero of the state but of the country. He has performed all his duties with great responsibility.â He pointed out that the five-time MP was known for his punctuality and dedication towards the stateâs people.Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya said Hira Singh Bisht was one of the pillars of Congress in the state and his demise is a big loss for the party as well as people.In addition to the Irrigation Bill, 2026, other bills tabled included Uttarakhand Investment and Infrastructure (Development and Regulation) (Amendment) Bill 2026, Uttarakhand Fire and Emergency Services Bill- 2026, Uttarakhand Minority Education Act (Amendment) Bill 2026, Uttarakhand Private Universities (2nd Amendment) Bill 2026, Uttarakhand Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill 2026 and Uttarakhand Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) 2nd Bill, 2026.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news.
